documents.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
documents.abstract: As severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms.

documents.title: The pharmacological potential and metabolic risks of Xiaojin Pill in sorafenib-resistant papillary thyroid carcinoma: an integrated network analysis.
documents.abstract: Sorafenib resistance limits the efficacy of treatments for advanced papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). The antitumor potential of Xiaojin Pill (XJP) has been demonstrated, yet its mechanisms potentially implicated in sorafenib resistance and combinational toxicological risks remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the molecular mechanisms through which XJP may act on signaling pathways implicated in sorafenib resistance, and to assess its combinational toxicological risks during co-administration with sorafenib.

documents.title: GolgiFold: A Structural Predictome of Human Golgi Protein Complexes.
documents.abstract: The Golgi apparatus is a central hub for protein secretion and endolysosomal biogenesis, coordinating protein and vesicular trafficking pathways that maintain cellular homeostasis. Although hundreds of proteins associate with the Golgi, molecular assemblies have been defined for only a subset. Such well-characterized complexes have provided fundamental insights into Golgi trafficking, protein processing, and homeostasis, suggesting that systematic mapping of the broader Golgi interactome would uncover unrecognized components and regulatory mechanisms. Here, we systematically interrogate Golgi
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Structural clustering across the tree of life reveals candidate Asgard-eukaryote homologs and a shared expansion of solenoids.
documents.abstract: Asgard archaea are the closest known prokaryotic relatives of eukaryotes, and their genomes encode many eukaryotic signature proteins (ESPs), homologs of proteins associated with eukaryotic cellular complexity. Because deep divergence limits sequence-based homology detection, structure-based searches are increasingly used to expand the ESP repertoire, but they start from individual Asgard proteins rather than the families those proteins belong to. Here we took a complementary, family-level approach, profiling the taxonomic composition of 1.89 million structural clusters from the AFESM database
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Discovery of benzimidazole-based selective α-glucosidase inhibitors with an uncompetitive mode of action: synthesis, biological assays and computational studies.
documents.abstract: A series of thirteen 1-(benzyloxy)-2-phenyl-1H-benzo[d]imidazole derivatives was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as α-glucosidase inhibitors. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that the presence of a chlorine atom at the C-6 position of the benzimidazole core, combined with suitable substituents on the pendant aromatic rings, was associated with relevant α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. Among the series, compounds 6 and 13 emerged as the most potent derivatives showing IC50 values of 32.35 μM and 15.70 μM, respectively, and greater potency than acarbose (IC50 = 139 μM) un

documents.title: Development of CYP8B1-specific inhibitors for metabolic diseases.
documents.abstract: Changes in bile acids (BAs) balance lead to various metabolic diseases, yet current treatment options targeting these changes remain severely limited. CYP8B1 (cytochrome P450, family 8, subfamily B, polypeptide 1) is a liver-exclusive enzyme that controls the synthesis of 12α-hydroxylated (12α-OH) BAs. Inhibiting CYP8B1 is an attractive therapeutic strategy for attenuating 12α-OH BA levels, remodeling the gut microbiota and thereby ameliorating metabolic diseases. CYP8B1-specific inhibitors are currently lacking due to structural similarities between the active site of CYP8B1 and other CYPs, a
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Free-Energy and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Ser195 and Thr195 Rotameric States in Thrombin.
documents.abstract: Ser195 is highly conserved as the catalytic nucleophile in trypsin-like serine proteases, yet the molecular basis for the strong preference for serine over the chemically similar threonine residue remains unclear. Here, we used well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond-long molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize the conformational energetics of S195 and T195 in thrombin. Well-tempered metadynamics revealed distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes in both the apo and the ligand-bound systems. In the apo state, S195 preferentially occupied a lower-angle rotameric state, while T195
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Edge-Aware Graph Attention Networks for Interpreting Biophysical Mechanisms from Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
documents.abstract: Graph attention networks (GATs) are emerging as powerful aritficial intelligence (AI) tools for learning biomolecular dynamics, yet extracting mechanistic insight from learned attention remains challenging. Here, we present an interpretable AI approach that combines molecular dynamics prediction with mechanistic interpretation through attention-derived communication networks. We develop three edge-aware GAT models - Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, and Edge-Gated - that differ in how edge information is incorporated during message passing. Relative to a standard GAT, our edge-aware models impr

documents.title: Structural Basis for Angiotensin II Type I Receptor G Protein-biased Signaling.
documents.abstract: Biased agonism at the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) offers a promising strategy for developing safer cardiovascular therapeutics. While β-arrestin-biased agonism has been extensively investigated, G protein-biased signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we report structures of AT1R coupled to G protein and either the endogenous agonist angiotensin II (AngII) or the G protein-biased agonist TRV055. The ligands adopt similar overall poses, with coordinated rearrangements extending from the orthosteric pocket to the intracellular surface. The structures provide a detailed view of a TM7
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: AT1R-Selective Negative Allosteric Modulator Targeting the Epitope for Pathogenic Autoantibody Activation.
documents.abstract: A major therapeutic strategy for managing cardiovascular and renal diseases is the use of angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs). These drugs block both pathogenic and physiological signaling by the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) by preventing angiotensin II (AngII) binding to orthosteric pocket in transmembrane portion of AT1R. However, in many autoimmune diseases, AT1R activation is chronically driven by pathogenic autoantibody binding to a distinct extracellular surface located allosteric site. Currently, there are no allosteric inhibitors of AT1R available to mechanistically prevent t
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: A computational-experimental strategy identifies K-7174 against African swine fever.
documents.abstract: African swine fever (ASF), caused by the African swine fever virus (ASFV), poses a catastrophic threat to global swine production due to the absence of effective vaccines or therapeutics. Targeting the virally encoded RNA polymerase (RNAP), which is essential for viral transcription, offers a promising antiviral strategy. Capitalizing on our previously resolved high-resolution structure of ASFV RNAP, we conducted a rigorous structure-based virtual screening of two compound libraries (T001 and LF1000) to identify selective inhibitors. From 100 candidates validated in vitro, nine compounds ident

documents.title: Structure-based prediction reveals FAM105A as an African swine fever virus I215L interactor.
documents.abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) causes a fatal hemorrhagic disease in pigs, leading to severe economic losses worldwide. The viral ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme I215L (E2) is critical for ASFV replication and modulation of host antiviral responses. Host deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs) bind to E2 enzymes to inhibit the transfer of ubiquitin. In this study, we systematically screened 34 swine DUBs using HDOCK docking and AlphaFold3 modeling, identifying FAM105A as the most probable interactor. Co-immunoprecipitation assay validated the interaction between I215L and FAM105A. Structural analyses r

documents.title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization.
documents.abstract: Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with s

documents.title: Integrating noncanonical amino acids and synthetic cofactors for the development of artificial metalloenzymes.
documents.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes harness the sophisticated synergy between canonical amino acids and metal cofactors to catalyze life-sustaining reactions. However, the limited chemical diversity of the twenty standard amino acids often restricts non-natural transformations. To overcome these constraints, artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) integrate synthetic cofactors into protein scaffolds to enable unnatural catalytic functions. This review highlights how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) bridge the gap between natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry. We examine genetic code expansion and co

documents.title: The evolutionary conserved protein-RNA interface formed by the cell-fate regulator Bicaudal-C.
documents.abstract: Bicaudal-C (Bicc1) is an essential cell-fate regulator that guides the animal body plan during early development and maintains organ homeostasis in adults. It does so by binding specific mRNA targets and regulating their translation, yet the molecular basis of mRNA target selection has remained unclear. Here, we combined experimental and computational approaches to define the Bicc1-RNA interaction. In vitro binding experiments with wild-type and mutant RNA substrates identified the RNA features recognized by Bicc1, while protein-RNA XL-MS-a UV-crosslinking approach coupled to LC-MS/MS-pinpoint

documents.title: Acetyl tributyl citrate induces neuronal ferroptosis through ATM-associated disruption of iron and redox homeostasis.
documents.abstract: Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) is widely used as a non-phthalate plasticizer, raising concerns about its potential health effects. Although emerging evidence suggests that ATBC may adversely affect the nervous system, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Given the critical role of ferroptosis in neuronal injury, this study investigated whether ferroptosis contributes to ATBC-induced neuronal injury and explored the potential involvement of ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) in this process.

documents.title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis.
documents.abstract: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether con

documents.title: NADPH-specific meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from the archaeon Pyrococcus sp. stereoselectively aminates α-keto acids using NADH.
documents.abstract: Enzymatic asymmetric D-amination of carbonyl compounds and keto acids is of great interest in biotechnology. Stable D-stereoselective NAD-dependent dehydrogenases are required for the synthesis of D-amino acids from α-keto acids, because they can use ammonium ion as the amino group donor and allow high product yield via coenzyme recycling. However, these enzymes are rare in nature. Here, we describe the first archaeal meso-diaminopimelate dehydrogenase from Pyrococcus sp. (PyrDAPDH). The enzyme is active with either NADP(H) or NAD(H) and catalyzes reductive amination of various α-keto acids an

documents.title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening.
documents.abstract: The receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein mediates viral entry through its interaction with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an attractive target for antiviral intervention. However, the broad and relatively shallow ACE2-binding interface presents a challenge for small-molecule inhibitor discovery. In this study, we explored conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface as potential druggable sites for small-molecule inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Structure-based virtual screening was pe

documents.title: Toward the Rational Design of Tailored Ligands for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins through NMR.
documents.abstract: Understanding the driving forces governing the interactions between intrinsically disordered proteins and their potential ligands represents a key step toward the rational design of drugs targeting this type of proteins. Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to achieve detailed atom-resolved information toward this ambitious goal. We present here a set of differently functionalized calix[4]arene-based multivalent ligands designed to target different regions of the well-characterized intrinsically disordered protein α-synuclein. Dedicated NMR experiments extended
documents.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

documents.title: From molecular pathways to nanocarrier design: a translational framework for lipid-based nanoparticles in Alzheimer's disease.
documents.abstract: Alzheimer's disease, being a complicated neurodegenerative disoder affects cognitive as well as memory functions. Characterised by amyloid-β aggregation, along with tau hyperphosphorylation, and cholinergic dysfunction, this disease is also associated with oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Conventional clinical interventions, like acetylcholinesterase inhibitors and novel monoclonal antibodies predominantly rely on symptomatic alleviation of symptoms. Nevertheless, these conventional treatments come across considerable constraints, like temporary effectiveness, lesser therapeutic reach d

documents.title: Cross-Linking Simulation at Metal Oxide-Thermoset Interfaces Using Quantum Chemical and Molecular Dynamics Methods.
documents.abstract: Understanding how oxidized metal surfaces catalyze the curing of epoxy resins is essential in improving the reliabilities of epoxy-metal oxide interfaces in multimaterial systems. The catalytic effects of hydroxylated oxidized tin metal (SnO2) surfaces on the cross-linking of epoxy resins were investigated using a hybrid approach that combined quantum chemical calculations with molecular dynamics simulations, wherein the reaction kinetics were modeled using Monte Carlo techniques. Analyzing the reaction pathways and spatial distributions at different hydroxylation levels revealed that fully hy

documents.title: Cytoplasmic Expression of Papain Isozymes in Engineered Escherichia coli for Substrate Selectivity and Computational Insights.
documents.abstract: Challenges in isolating individual papain isozymes from papaya latex and in producing full-length, correctly folded, and soluble recombinant papain isozymes in Escherichia coli have limited detailed investigations into their distinct enzymatic properties and substrate specificities. In this study, we report the successful high-yield cytoplasmic expression of papain, protease omega, proteinase IV (pro-IV), and chymopapains I, II, and III in engineered E. coli SHuffle strains and a comprehensive investigation of their distinct biochemical and computational mechanistic insights. Building upon our

documents.title: Poké: Fast and Reliable Neural-Network-Based Identification of Protein Ligandable Sites.
documents.abstract: Accurate identification of ligandable pockets is of key relevance for structure-based drug design; however, their identification remains challenging, particularly for cryptic sites that become accessible only upon conformational changes. Here, we introduce Poké, a high-performance pocket scouting tool that combines energetic mapping with a neural-network-based ligandability score, enabling rapid and reliable binding site detection in both static structures and long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories. Poké identifies low-energy regions on protein surfaces through probe-based grid en

documents.title: Weighted Views Representation with Multi-Head Coulomb Attention for Molecular Property Prediction.
documents.abstract: We extend the weighted-views molecular featurization framework (d'Avezac, Botts, Mohlenkamp, and Zunger, 2011) by enriching it with single-atom properties and Coulomb pair information. We use these enriched views within a machine-learning architecture incorporating shared Transformers whose attention scores directly incorporate Coulomb interactions, weighted aggregation of view outputs, and a final prediction neural network. We demonstrate performance competitive with the state-of-the-art on the QM7 atomization energy benchmark (regression), ranking enantiomers by their docking scores (trained

documents.title: OPC3/LEW: A New Flexible Three-Site Water Model to Simulate Low-Electrostatic Environments.
documents.abstract: One of the main goals of computational simulations is to closely reproduce the environmental conditions in which biomolecules perform their physiological functions. However, the choice of water model is often based more on computational cost than on its effect on the molecular environment, as is the case with membrane proteins. These systems fulfill their biological function in low-polarity molecular environments that the most common or currently available water models do not reproduce accurately. In this work, we present a new flexible water model with three interaction sites that accurately

documents.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors.
documents.abstract: Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. Ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. This work leverages machine learning to predict four key transport properties in amorphous polymer electrolytes using a molecular dynamics data set of more than 6,000 polymer electrolyte systems. These are i

documents.title: Structural basis for saccharide binding by human RNase 2/EDN: Insights into its potential lectin-like properties.
documents.abstract: Human RNase 2, also named the eosinophil-derived neurotoxin (EDN), is a secretory protein of the vertebrate-specific RNase A superfamily involved in antiviral and proinflammatory cell response. Identifying ligand-binding pockets in EDN is thus relevant to structure-based drug design. By X-ray crystallography we first identified a conserved site at the protein surface binding to carboxylic anion molecules: malonate, tartrate and citrate. Searching for potential biomolecules rich in anion groups and considering previous report of EDN interaction to glycosaminoglycans, we explored the protein bin

documents.title: Enterovirus 2C Protein Drug Design, Assay Development, and Drug Resistance Studies.
documents.abstract: In this Account, we describe our efforts to establish enteroviral 2C as a tractable target for antiviral drug discovery by integrating medicinal chemistry, molecular pharmacology, resistance profiling, structural modeling, and assay development. Rather than relying solely on conventional phenotypic high-throughput screening, our initial studies focused on the rational optimization of reported 2C inhibitors identified from a drug-repurposing campaign. This strategy led to quinoline-based antivirals with substantially improved potency and selectivity against enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), providing e

documents.title: From structure prediction to ligand-target recognition: expanding the reach of AlphaFold in natural product research.
documents.abstract: Natural products constitute a structurally diverse reservoir of bioactive molecules and remain an important source of lead compounds for drug discovery. However, the limited availability of structural information on pharmacological targets and biomolecular interactions continues to hinder mechanism elucidation and structure-guided optimization, particularly for complex natural products such as bioactive peptides, proteinaceous natural products, and natural molecular glues. Recent advances in AlphaFold have transformed structural biology by enabling high-confidence prediction of protein structu

documents.title: HEDGEHOG: hierarchical evaluation of drug generators through rigorous filtration.
documents.abstract: Generative molecular models can support early drug discovery by proposing new candidate compounds de novo. In practice, useful candidates must balance target-relevant activity, physicochemical properties, and other multiparameter design constraints. However, standard metrics commonly used to evaluate molecular generators only weakly reflect whether the generated compounds are medicinally plausible and suitable for downstream computation. This can produce an incomplete view of model performance and inefficient use of computational resources. We introduce HEDGEHOG, a configurable six-stage evalu

documents.title: Structure-based discovery of novel BCL-XL inhibitors through molecular docking and key interaction-guided virtual screening.
documents.abstract: BCL-XL, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL-2 protein family, is an attractive therapeutic target for overcoming apoptosis resistance in cancer. However, the large, shallow, and predominantly hydrophobic nature of its BH3-binding groove has complicated the discovery of potent, drug-like small-molecule inhibitors. Here, we employed structure-based virtual screening with key interaction constraints to identify novel BCL-XL inhibitor scaffolds with relatively low molecular weights (MWs). Approximately 312,000 drug-like compounds were docked into the BH3-binding groove, and the top-ranked molecule

documents.title: Psychotropic Drug GST Interactions: In Vitro Inhibition, Molecular Docking, and Translational Potential in Cancer Therapy.
documents.abstract: Psychotropic drugs are widely used to treat mental disorders, but they also influence cellular pathways linked to cancer. One key enzyme, Glutathione S-transferase (GST), is involved in detoxification and drug resistance in tumors, making it a potential target in cancer therapy. This study examined the effects of selected psychotropic agents aripiprazole, fluoxetine hydrochloride, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate on GST activity derived from equine liver. Enzyme kinetics were assessed in vitro using 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) as the substrate and ethacrynic acid (Kᵢ = 4.7
documents.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

documents.title: Cytotoxic Activity and Molecular Docking Studies of ONNO Type Salophen Schiff Base Metal Complexes.
documents.abstract: A Schiff base ligand (H2L) was synthesized through the condensation of 3,5-dibromo-2-hydroxybenzaldehyde with 1,2-phenylenediamine and subsequently complexed with Cu(II), Ni(II), Pt(II), Fe(II), and Pd(II) ions. Synthesized compounds were examined using FT-IR, UV-Vis, NMR, mass, elemental analysis, molar conductivity, and magnetic susceptibility. The H2L and transition metal complexes were tested for their cytotoxic activity potential against human liver carcinoma (HepG2) and lung adenocarcinoma (A549) cell lines. The cytotoxic activities of compounds were determined based on their IC50 values

documents.title: From "undruggable" to tractable: Therapeutic advances targeting Kristen rat sarcoma viral homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C)-mutant cancers and emerging resistance mechanisms.
documents.abstract: This review explains the evolution of Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog glycine to cysteine mutation at codon 12 (KRAS G12C) from an "undruggable" target to a manageable oncogenic driver in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). While first-generation inhibitors have significantly improved patient care, the emergence of complex resistance mechanisms necessitates a shift toward precision-driven combination therapies and advanced computational drug discovery. The KRAS G12C mutation is a primary driver in approximately 8.9% of NSCLC patients, particularly smokers. The development of covalen

documents.title: A split nozzle and two-protein chain-like fibers define the tail architecture of Pseudomonas aeruginosa podophage A1002.
documents.abstract: Phage therapy offers unique advantages against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. However, high-resolution structural studies of phages targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa-a top-seven global pathogen-particularly podophages, remain severely limited, directly impeding structure-based development of novel antimicrobials. In this study, we utilize cryo-EM to resolve the high-resolution intact structure of mature phage A1002, a podophage infecting carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa. Based on density maps combined with AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified 11 structural protein components from the head to

documents.title: Molecular force gates regulate mechanical transmission across the nuclear envelope.
documents.abstract: The LINC (linker of nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton) complex is a central mechanotransductive apparatus that physically couples cytoskeletal forces to the nuclear interior, thereby regulating nuclear architecture, chromatin organization, and downstream signaling. Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we identify and characterize 'force gates' within the LINC complex - structural interactions that maintain mechanical connectivity under load. documents.title: Identification of Neuroinflammation-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: An Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Approach.
documents.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a liver disease that progresses and may be connected to neuroinflammation, though the specific molecular mechanisms are not yet understood. The objective of this research was to explore candidate diagnostic biomarkers related to neuroinflammation-associated gene programs for MASH through integrated bioinformatics and machine learning, as a hypothesis-generating study.

documents.title: Carbonic anhydrase 4 restrains dual TLR4-NF-κB/IRF3 innate immune signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in methotrexate-induced pulmonary fibrosis.
documents.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX)-induced pulmonary fibrosis (MTX-PF) is the most severe and frequently irreversible manifestation of MTX pulmonary toxicity, yet the molecular target and signaling circuitry linking drug exposure to fibrosis remain undefined, hampering diagnosis and targeted intervention.

documents.title: Integrated pharmacology and validation reveal Formononetin upregulates GSTM2 to modulate prostate cancer immune microenvironment via ROS/STAT3-driven chemokine reprogramming.
documents.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is responsible for a substantial proportion of male cancer cases worldwide. Biochemical recurrence (BCR) representing a critical challenge in its disease management. Formononetin, a natural isoflavone derived from traditional Chinese medicine, has demonstrated potential anticancer properties. We sought to determine the translational potential of Formononetin-targeted molecules in PCa.

documents.title: Mutation-induced structural and dynamic perturbations at the IL-17A-IL-17RA interface: Therapeutic insights from multi-replicate molecular dynamics simulations.
documents.abstract: The interaction between Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and its receptor IL-17RA plays a key role in pro-inflammatory signal transduction and is implicated in the pathogenesis of inflammatory autoimmune diseases. Blocking this protein-protein interaction is a major approach to developing therapeutic agents to inhibit IL-17A-induced signaling. Predicting the consequences of mutations on structure and function in proteins can be accomplished by using computational methods, which are relatively inexpensive and rapid compared with experimental methods. Here, we used a multidimensional in silico approach

documents.title: Quercetin ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced placental dysfunction by modulating the AGE-RAGE-associated oxidative and inflammatory signaling network.
documents.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) induces placental structural and functional disturbances associated with dysregulated AGE-RAGE/ROS signaling and inflammatory responses. Existing flavonoid-related studies merely observed changes in pathway protein levels, lacking direct experimental proof of molecular binding between candidate compounds and core receptors. This study aimed to investigate the potential involvement of RAGE in the protective effects of quercetin and to characterize the associated AGE-RAGE/ROS/NF-κB-related signaling changes in GDM placental injury.

documents.title: Kurarinol A from Sophora flavescens suppresses hepatic stellate cell activation via the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB pathway.
documents.abstract: Sophora flavescens is traditionally used in TCM and Miao/Mongolian/Yi ethnomedicines for hepatobiliary disorders, yet its bioactive flavonoid constituents and mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the anti-hepatic fibrosis efficacy, mechanism, and target of the ethyl acetate fraction (EAF) from S. flavescens and its key lavandulyl flavonoid kurarinol A (KA).

documents.title: A Tanshinone IIA Sulfonate Derivative Targets USP21 to Induce SCD1 Degradation, Suppressing NSCLC Metabolism and Enhancing Antitumor Immunity.
documents.abstract: Background: The deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific peptidase 21 (USP21) is a key regulator of tumor metabolism and immune homeostasis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Its aberrant activation drives malignant growth, metabolic reprogramming and immune resistance, yet specific USP21 inhibitors for NSCLC therapy remain scarce. We aimed to develop a selective USP21 inhibitor, define its immunometabolic mechanism, and validate its anti-tumor and immunotherapy-sensitizing effects in NSCLC. Methods: We performed structure-based hierarchical virtual screening of a Food and Drug Administration (FD

documents.title: Structure-based minimization of a high-mobility group protein B1 (HMGB1) B box peptide uncouples anti-NETotic activity and anti-biofilm function.
documents.abstract: We previously showed that human HMGB1 has anti-biofilm activity localized to a 97-amino-acid B-Box-derived peptide (mB Box-97), engineered with a C106S mutation to reduce HMGB1's proinflammatory properties while retaining anti-biofilm function. This peptide also suppresses NETosis by inhibiting neutrophil protein kinase C (PKC) activity. documents.title: Discovery of Galangin Derivatives as a Potential T-cell Leukemia Virus 1 Protease Inhibitor Through Chemoinformatics Approaches
p70S6K as a Potential Anti-COVID-19 Target: Insights from Wet Bench and In Silico Studies
documents.abstract: The onset of SARS-CoV-2 infection in 2019 sparked a global COVID-19 pandemic. This infection is marked by a significant rise in both viral and host kinase activity. Our primary objective was to identify a pivotal host kinase essential for COVID-19 infection and the associated phenomenon of the cytokine storm, which may lead to long-term COVID-19 complications irrespective of viral genetic variations.
